label: Jaan Tallinn
note: SFF’s table names him as the funder, alone or with Dustin Moskovitz, on those METR, Apollo Research, Palisade Research and Lightcone rows shown here whose funder was checked, and Anthropic’s 2021 announcement says he led its Series A. FLI’s finances page says he has donated to FLI and sits on its board.

label: Survival and Flourishing Fund (SFF)
note: SFF publishes recommendations made for its funders. The lines drawn from SFF on this map are those recommendations, except the line to MIRI, which shows the figure MIRI’s own contributors page lists for SFF. The recommendations are not payments out of a fund of its own, and the record does not show what was paid on them. Its table gives each row a round, an amount and a named funder: Jaan Tallinn on the rows where the funder was checked, and in 2026 also Dustin Moskovitz. An amount marked ‡ is a matching pledge, which SFF’s 2026 page says depends on the recipient raising outside funds. Its 2026 page lists Scott Alexander among the recommenders who agreed to be named.

label: Dustin Moskovitz
note: Anthropic’s announcement of 28 May 2021 names him among the participants in its Series A, with no amount. SFF’s table names him, with Jaan Tallinn, as a funder on its 2026 rows for Apollo Research, Palisade Research and Lightcone Infrastructure.

label: Coefficient Giving (formerly Open Philanthropy)
note: Its grants to Redwood Research, Apollo Research, Palisade Research and Lightcone are taken here from relays of its grant pages (Donations List Website, Longterm Wiki), from an aggregator (Evaluator Bench) and from a press report (TNW), not from its own database; those to Epoch AI from Epoch’s transparency page; those to MIRI and FHI from MIRI’s pages and an Oxford Martin School announcement. Its own announcement of 18 Nov 2025: “Today, Open Philanthropy is becoming Coefficient Giving.” Good Ventures, the foundation of Cari Tuna and Dustin Moskovitz, calls it “our primary philanthropic advisor”. People ties on the record: Anthropic's announcement of 29 May 2024 says Luke Muehlhauser stepped down from its board “to focus on his work at Open Philanthropy”; Holden Karnofsky, Open Philanthropy's co-founder, is listed by Harvard's Berkman Klein Center (Oct 2025) as a Member of Technical Staff at Anthropic.

words.speaker: Open Philanthropy (grant record)
words.quote: $370,000 represents an "exit grant" for Lightcone’s other work.
words.source: Lightcone Infrastructure - General Support (2023) (Open Philanthropy grant record, as mirrored by LongtermWiki)

disputes.what: The Alignment Research Center wrote on 15 November 2022 that its $1.25M FTX Foundation grant “morally (if not legally) belongs to FTX customers or creditors” and that it would return it. Its 2024 update says the grant went back to the FTX bankruptcy estate, less legal and administrative expenses.

The FTX Future Fund’s team announced on 11 November 2022 that it had resigned. It wrote that “it looks likely that there are many committed grants that the Future Fund will be unable to honor” and cited “fundamental questions about the legitimacy and integrity of the business operations”.
disputes.source: The FTX Future Fund team has resigned (EA Forum)

disputes.what: Cointelegraph reported on 13 March 2026 that Vitalik Buterin wrote he had expected FLI to cash out “at most $10-25M” of his 2021 token gift, that it “managed to cash out something like $500M”, and that he was wary of “large-scale coordinated political action with big money pools”.
disputes.response: In an update of 16 March 2026 to the same article, FLI’s president and CEO Anthony Aguirre said FLI has “immense respect for Vitalik’s views on AI safety” and that the two remain aligned on some specific approaches.

label: Thiel Foundation
note: MIRI's Top Contributors page lists it under Past Contributors at $1,627,000 and gives no year. Whether the pledges and matches recorded under Peter Thiel's own name are part of that figure is not established here, so the amounts are not to be added.

label: Founders Fund
note: Venture firm. In the rounds recorded here (OpenAI 2023 and 2025, Anthropic 2026, Cognition 2024) the sources give the round's size or its lead investors, not Founders Fund's own share.

label: Marc Andreessen
note: The Transformer tracker lists him as an individual donor to Leading the Future (employer: Andreessen Horowitz) at $25.00M across two filings. The tracker's figure is a running total across filings, not a single gift.

words.speaker: Marc Andreessen
words.quote: The grant was intended to support independent AI research, and the results have been wonderful.
words.source: DL News, 17 October 2024, quoting his post on X

disputes.what: After a memecoin promoted by the Truth Terminal account surged, DL News reported on 17 October 2024 that Marc Andreessen said he had nothing to do with the token and did not own any of it.
disputes.response: DL News quotes his post describing the $50K as a “no-string-attached unconditional research grant”.

label: Ben Horowitz
note: The Transformer tracker lists him as an individual donor to Leading the Future (employer: Andreessen Horowitz) at $25.00M across two filings, a running total and not a single gift.

label: Andreessen Horowitz (a16z)
note: The pages read for the gifts to Leading the Future (the NOTUS report, the Bloomberg report and the Transformer tracker) name Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz as individual donors. None names A16Z Capital Management LLC as the contributor.

label: Greg Brockman
note: Gizmodo's report of 1 October 2026 calls Greg Brockman OpenAI's president and relays OpenAI's statement that his engagement was “in a personal capacity, not on behalf of the company”.

disputes.what: The New York Times reported on 30 September 2026, as relayed by Gizmodo, that Greg Brockman would not give a second $25 million that the super PAC said he and his wife had promised.
disputes.response: A June 2026 Slack message from him, as reported by the Times and relayed by Gizmodo, reads: “We’ve donated $25m so far, and have no plans to donate more at this time.” OpenAI said his engagement was “in a personal capacity, not on behalf of the company”.
disputes.source: Gizmodo, 1 October 2026, citing the New York Times

label: Leading the Future (super PAC)
note: The Transformer tracker, compiled from FEC filings, lists it as the top donor to two other committees, Think Big and American Mission. Zac Moffatt and Josh Vlasto issued a statement for it, quoted in a NOTUS report of 30 January 2026.

words.quote: Candidates who grasp the stakes can expect us to help elevate that message,

label: Public First Action
note: Anthropic's February 2026 post calls it “a new bipartisan 501(c)(4)”; its July 2026 post says Anthropic's donations “cannot be used to influence the election of any candidate”. The Transformer tracker lists it as a donor to two political committees. How its funds are kept apart was not established from the sources read.

label: Jobs and Democracy PAC
note: The Transformer tracker also lists Public First, a super PAC with its own tracker page, as a donor to this committee at $4.05M.

label: American Technology Excellence Project (super PAC)
note: A New York Times report of 18 February 2026, read at GV Wire, says its money is expected to flow on to Forge the Future Project and Making Our Tomorrow.

label: Mobilizing Economic Transformation Across California (super PAC)

words.speaker: Kanishka Narayan, UK AI minister
words.quote: When you're reliant on someone else's technology, you have to be clear-eyed about the permanence of any outcome.
words.source: UK given access to safety-test latest AI models, minister says (Reuters, in The Star)

label: US National Institute of Mental Health
Frontier Model Forum
note: Body whose About page says it 'is funded by fees from its member firms' and gives no fee levels. Its AI Safety Fund page names Anthropic, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI as its four founders; no page listing current members was checked.

label: AI Safety Fund
note: The Frontier Model Forum calls it a '$10 million+ initiative established in October 2023'. A November 2024 update reports over $3 million to twelve grantees; a December 2025 announcement, more than $5 million to 11 grantees. No source relates the figures.

label: The Alignment Project
note: Fund for outside alignment research, led by the UK AI Security Institute and presented on its site. A UK government release of 19 February 2026 says over £27 million is available, backing some 60 projects. The same release lists Anthropic in the coalition, with Amazon Web Services and Schmidt Sciences, and does not say what Anthropic contributed.

label: Lightcone Commons (funding platform)
note: A funding platform announced by Lightcone's chief executive in July 2026. Its “evaluators” recommend grants to funders and are not the bodies that test AI models elsewhere on this map. He wrote that "Evaluators are paid 2% of recommendations, and we charge a 3% platform fee" and, in November 2026, that "We don’t decide to make specific grants."

words.speaker: Oliver Habryka, chief executive, Lightcone Infrastructure
words.quote: Lightcone Commons is not a foundation. We don’t decide to make specific grants.
words.source: Lightcone Commons: Round 1 complete, Round 2 underway (LessWrong)

words.speaker: Oliver Habryka, chief executive, Lightcone Infrastructure
words.quote: Evaluators are paid 2% of recommendations, and we charge a 3% platform fee.

words.source: Lightcone Commons: Round 1 complete, Round 2 underway (LessWrong)

disputes.what: Nectome wrote on 3 November 2026 that Lightcone Commons "invested ~$3M" in it; its post names no individual funders.
disputes.response: Lightcone's chief executive wrote on 10 November 2026 that "Lightcone Commons is not a foundation" and that "Lightcone Commons staff do not decide what grants get made", and asked recipients to stop saying "Lightcone Commons funded us".
disputes.source: Lightcone Commons: Round 1 complete, Round 2 underway (LessWrong, 10 November 2026)

words.speaker: Aubrey de Grey

label: Employees of Anthropic and OpenAI (personal donations)
note: A group, not one person: staff of AI companies giving from their own holdings, as the recipient reports it. By the recipient’s account it received no revenue directly from AI developers as organisations.

label: FTX and Alameda (Sam Bankman-Fried)
note: Anthropic's own announcement says its 2022 Series B was led by Sam Bankman-Fried, then FTX's chief executive. After FTX failed, its bankruptcy estate sold the Anthropic shares in 2024 (reported by The Block from court documents).

label: Amazon
note: Invested in Anthropic from 2023 and sells it compute through AWS. Leverage Shares, reading Anthropic's registration statement, says the S-1 “names Amazon and Google as holders who will each own more than 5% of the company after the IPO”, mostly in non-voting shares, with Amazon's ownership capped at 12%.

label: NVIDIA
note: Committed on 18 November 2025 to invest up to $10 billion in Anthropic, and is reported as a buyer of about $10 billion of its stock at the offering price.

label: Spark Capital
note: Led Anthropic's $450 million Series C (2023).

label: SK Telecom
note: Invested $100 million in Anthropic in 2023, with a partnership on a telecom language model.

label: Menlo Ventures
note: Reported in December 2023 as leading talks for a $750 million investment in Anthropic; named by Anthropic among participants in its Series E (2025).

label: ICONIQ
note: Led Anthropic's Series F (2025) and co-led its Series G and Series H (2026), by Anthropic's own announcements.

label: GIC (Singapore)
note: Describes itself as “the world’s first non-commodity-based sovereign wealth fund”. Named by Anthropic as an investor in its Series F, a lead of its Series G and a co-lead of its Series H.

label: Coatue
note: Named by Anthropic as an investor in its Series F, a lead of its Series G and a co-lead of its Series H.

label: MGX
note: An Abu Dhabi investment company, named by Anthropic as a co-lead of its Series G and an investor in its Series H.

label: Qatar Investment Authority
note: Named by Anthropic among the investors in its Series F (2025) and its Series G (2026).

label: Altimeter Capital
note: One of four leads of Anthropic's $65 billion Series H (May 2026).

label: Dragoneer
note: Co-led Anthropic's Series G and was one of four leads of its Series H (2026).

label: Greenoaks
note: One of four leads of Anthropic's $65 billion Series H (May 2026).

note: Named by Anthropic among the investors in its Series G and as one of four leads of its Series H (2026).
